videos.title: AI Held Up Stocks. What’s Holding Up AI?
videos.description:
AI revenue has to catch up with data center spending. Households have kept spending faster than their wages grow. In this Excess Returns Weekly Wrap, Jack Forehand and Matt Zeigler ask what happens if stock gains and easy refinancing can no longer help close those gaps.

Michael Howell explains why investors can feel a squeeze even while the global pool of money is still growing. Bob Elliott puts a number on the revenue AI labs would need to justify the buildout, while Dave Nadig and Cameron Dawson look at the same bet from the chipmakers’ side. Intel beat earnings expectations and its shares still fell. What kind of growth had investors already paid for?

John Davi brings the question back to the portfolio. An investor can trim exposure to the biggest stocks and still wind up with a sector bet they never intended. Aahan Menon brings it home to the household budget, where rising stock and home values have helped consumers spend more of each paycheck.

Topics covered:
- Michael Howell on why the pace of global liquidity growth matters for stocks
- Bob Elliott on the gap between AI labs’ revenue and the sales needed to pay for new capacity
- Dave Nadig on what Intel’s selloff after an earnings beat says about expectations
- Cameron Dawson on why chip earnings can peak even if data center spending keeps rising
- John Davi on pairing equal stock weights with sector controls to manage concentration
- Aahan Menon on how a lower saving rate has helped consumption outgrow wages
- Jac

videos.title: Why Market Fragility is Building into a Crisis in 2027  | Cem Karsan & Noel Smith
videos.description:
This episode is brought to you by Sarmaya Partners. Learn more about Sarmaya’s LENS ETF, their full data and comparison, including performance here: https://sarmayaetf.com/

Cem Karsan and Noel Smith, co-CIOs of Kai Asset Management, join OPM with Max Wiethe to dissect the volatility compression that is currently masking extreme dispersion across equity markets. Karsan explains why the current is one major catalyst away from a fat-tail Minsky moment, while Smith outlines the exact options strategies they are deploying to navigate the market's structural fragility. The duo also breaks down the macro shift toward populist, demand-side economics, predicting that structural inflation is here to stay and the value factor will crush growth investing in that environment. Finally, they reveal why an impending U.S. Treasury crisis will force the Federal Reserve to deploy massive quantitative easing, effectively bringing state-run intervention to U.S. equities to prevent a market collapse.
